courses.title: Canadian Legal System
courses.description: Covers key elements of the Canadian legal system including legal institutions, the Constitution, legislation, case law, courts and legal professions, legal pluralism in Canada, and the historical development of the Canadian legal system, together with an overview of selected: criminal law, administrative law, family law, tort law, and business law.

courses.title: Legal Research and Writing
courses.description: Designed to give students a solid foundation in legal research and writing skills. Provides students with an overview of how both legislation and case law are created, including consideration of the basic principles of legal analysis. Proper legal research techniques and strategies will be considered for both primary and secondary legal sources. Consideration will also be given to the many on-line legal research resources. Finally, students will receive instruction in the general principles of legal writing and apply these principles to different types of legal writing including analytical writing and the drafting of legal documents.

courses.title: Real Property I
courses.description: Involves the study of basic principles and statutory regimes which govern the institution of Real Property. Topics addressed will include: the legal concept of land, the nature of and rationale for property, transfer of interests in land, registration of title and the nature of the land title system, the acquisition of estates in land, co-ownership of land, and future interests.

courses.title: Topics in Legal Practice
courses.description: Builds on the theoretical understanding students have by exploring how the legal advisor assists clients in effectively dealing with their issues. Topics range from the purpose of legal professionals to developing sustainable strategies for the operation of a legal practice.
